glossary.Non-malignant: Not cancerous; it does not invade or spread.
glossary.Stromal: Relating to the supporting connective and muscle tissue of an organ.
glossary.Epithelial: Relating to the lining or glandular cells of an organ.
glossary.Proliferation: Rapid increase in the number of cells.
glossary.Hyperplasia: Enlargement of an organ due to an increased number of cells.
glossary.Dihydrotestosterone: A more potent form of testosterone that drives prostate growth.
glossary.Weak stream: Reduced force of the urine flow.
glossary.Intermittent flow: Urine flow that stops and starts.
glossary.Incomplete emptying: The feeling that the bladder is not empty after passing urine.
glossary.Frequency: Needing to pass urine more often than usual.
glossary.Urgency: A sudden, strong need to pass urine that is hard to delay.
glossary.Suprapubic: Just above the pubic bone, where a full bladder is felt.
glossary.Bladder stones: Hard mineral deposits that form in urine left standing in the bladder.
glossary.Urine dipstick: A reagent strip dipped in urine to detect blood, protein, nitrites and leucocytes.
glossary.Ejaculation: Release of semen, which can temporarily raise PSA.
glossary.Biopsy: Removing a small sample of tissue to examine under a microscope.
glossary.Ultrasound: An imaging scan using sound waves, here to measure urine left in the bladder.
glossary.Conservative: Managed without drugs or surgery, using lifestyle changes.
glossary.Dizziness: Feeling light-headed or unsteady, a common alpha-blocker side effect.
glossary.Falls: A history of falls makes the blood-pressure-lowering effect of alpha-blockers dangerous.
glossary.5-alpha-reductase inhibitor: Drug class, e.g. finasteride, that blocks conversion of testosterone to DHT and shrinks the prostate.
glossary.Impotence: Inability to achieve or keep an erection.
glossary.Darifenacin: An antimuscarinic drug that relaxes the bladder to reduce urgency and frequency.
glossary.Transurethral: Performed through the urethra, without an external cut.
glossary.Resection: Surgical removal of part of an organ.
glossary.Glandular epithelium: The secretory lining cells of the prostate gland.
glossary.Fibromuscular stroma: The fibrous and smooth muscle tissue that supports the prostate.
glossary.Proximal urethra: The part of the urethra nearest the bladder, running through the prostate.
glossary.Testosterone: The main male sex hormone, converted to DHT in the prostate.
glossary.Alpha-1 receptors: Adrenaline receptors that make smooth muscle contract.
glossary.Bladder neck: The funnel-shaped base of the bladder where it joins the urethra.
glossary.Smooth muscle: Involuntary muscle found in the prostate, bladder neck and blood vessels.
glossary.Hypertrophy: Enlargement of a muscle because each cell grows bigger.
glossary.Decompensation: Failure of an organ that had been coping with extra strain.
glossary.Residual urine: Urine left in the bladder after passing urine.
glossary.Prostate cancer: Malignant tumour of the prostate, usually in the peripheral zone.
glossary.Ultrasound bladder: Bladder scan measuring the post-void residual volume.
